criteria.no: No: the item is silent or only topical about the trait, or a backend does not implement Storage<T>.
criteria.unclear: Whether all three implement the same trait cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: Yes: all three backends implement the same Storage<T> trait.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` say that SQLite, Postgres and MySQL backends all implement the one shared Storage<T> trait? Judge presence only.

criteria.no: The item states no such plan, whether it complies, is silent, or only changes other parts of storage.
criteria.unclear: The item is ambiguous about whether every backend implements the shared trait.
criteria.yes: The item states such a plan.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` propose doing something that `anchor.statement` rules out? For this anchor that means a plan where the SQLite, Postgres and MySQL backends do not all implement the same Storage<T> trait, for example one backend using its own trait or functions. Silence about the trait is not a contradiction. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item touches neither the storage trait nor any of these storage backends, for example README edits about other features, CI, or dependency documentation.
criteria.unclear: The item's subject is too vague to place inside or outside the scope.
criteria.yes: The item defines or changes the storage trait or its documentation, or implements or changes a SQLite, Postgres or MySQL storage backend.

relevant.instructions: Is `item.text` within `anchor.scope`: work that defines the storage trait or implements a SQLite, Postgres or MySQL storage backend? An item that only adds a trait method, wires a connection pool, adds migrations for a backend, or documents the storage abstraction is within scope even if it never says which trait the backends implement. Judge scope only.
